verdict.rationale: Stagehand documents an `agent` that turns high-level tasks into fully autonomous browser workflows, with configurable max steps and agent fallbacks. Its Browserbase browsers run remotely with session replay, which fits unattended execution. However, nothing shows Stagehand itself scheduling, triggering, or hosting automations to run on their own in the background; the evidence covers invoked SDK runs (one-off execution), not recurring schedules. missing for 10: built-in scheduling/recurring triggers, documented background/unattended hosting of automations, independent hands-on corroboration of autonomous background runs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: `agent` turns high level tasks into **fully autonomous** browser workflows.
Use an agent fallback as a failsafe when a one step action unexpectedly becomes a multi-step flow.
Browserbase provides real-time visibility into your automation sessions
